title: A quadratic trend plus one Schwarzschild disc-crossing shape fits 22 ASASSN-14ko times at a high mass scale
abstract: We test whether a physical disc-crossing shape can replace the roughly 20-cycle sine in the ASASSN-14ko timing record when a secular quadratic trend is allowed. We use 22 published dip-equivalent times from 2007-2026. A free Kepler node shape gives chi-square 10.39 with a fixed 0.5-day scatter. An exact Schwarzschild shape gives 10.38 with six parameters, eccentricity 0.0787, a 19.77-event beat period and a mass scale of 6.15e8 solar masses at an adopted mean event period of 110 days. The opposite node lies 49.34-60.71 days later, so it cannot give the observed extra UV peak at 10-22 days through prompt emission with equal delays. Removing the infrared epoch or pre-2014 times, or adding the alternative DES 2013 time, retains the free-node branch. The first-order model fits worse at the common lower mass estimate; published mass estimates differ. This is an allowed timing template, not a mass measurement or a self-consistent evolving orbit. The quadratic trend and fixed orbital shape are separate terms. Code, source hashes, sensitivity fits, a conditional bootstrap and numerical checks are supplied.
